  Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
  What is a higher and degree apprenticeship?
  Higher apprenticeships involve studying at level 4, 5, 6 and 7. They can be suitable for those looking to progress from level 3 qualifications, including A-levels, advanced apprenticeships and T Levels.
  Degree apprenticeships are offered by universities and other higher education providers. They contain either a full degree or a degree-level qualification and go up to master’s level (which is post-
  graduate).


  Why aren’t level 2 and level 3 opportunities included in this guide?
  This listing is to promote higher and degree apprenticeship vacancies across England, therefore only levels 4 – 7 are included.
  You can find level 2 and 3 vacancies on Find an apprenticeship: gov.uk/apply-apprenticeship
  Sign up to receive the monthly Amazing Apprenticeships newsletter, Vacancy Snapshot, featuring the latest apprenticeship vacancies at all levels: amapps.uk/vacancies
